[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Web Accessibility (WCAG) and Usability Testing in Manual QA"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Introduction to Web Accessibility and WCAG"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Web accessibility ensures that digital platforms can be used by everyone, including people with visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive disabilities. As manual testers, verifying accessibility involves ensuring adherence to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), which are organized around four core principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust (POUR)."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Key WCAG Principles for Manual Testers"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Perceivable: Information and user interface components must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive. Key checks include alt text for images and sufficient color contrast ratios."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Operable: User interface components and navigation must be operable. Manual tests must verify complete keyboard navigation (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape) without trapping focus."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Understandable: Information and the operation of the user interface must be understandable. Check for clear error messages, predictable navigation, and readable text."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Robust: Content must be robust enough to be interpreted reliably by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies like screen readers."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Executing Manual Accessibility Testing"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Manual accessibility testing goes beyond automated scanners. To perform a robust manual accessibility test, testers must use native keyboard interactions, zoom functionalities up to 200% without loss of content, and screen readers such as NVDA or VoiceOver."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"<!-- Example of accessible HTML structure -->
<button aria-label="Close modal" onclick="closeModal()">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><!-- SVG Icon --></svg>
</button>"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Integrating Usability Testing"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While accessibility focuses on compliance with WCAG standards, usability testing evaluates how intuitive and efficient the product is for real users. Manual testers should evaluate task completion rates, user friction points, and overall layout clarity under various simulated user journeys."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Best Practices and Bug Reporting"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always document accessibility bugs with clear reproduction steps, specifying the exact WCAG success criterion violated (e.g., WCAG 2.1 - Criterion 1.4.3 Contrast)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Include details on assistive technology used (e.g., NVDA on Chrome) when logging screen reader issues."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining WCAG compliance checks with practical usability evaluations, manual testers ensure that applications are not only legally compliant but genuinely user-friendly for all audiences."}]
